transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Well, I came in because... I just can't seem to shake this thought I've been having. I've been an electrician for years, and I keep thinking that if all my experience couldn't keep my own brother safe, then... I'm just a danger to anybody who works with me. Or even the people living under my roof. It's just been weighing on me heavily, and I figured I needed to talk to someone.
When this thought comes up, do you feel driven to perform a specific action or mental ritual to prevent harm or reduce your anxiety?

No, I don't... I don't really do anything like that. I don't have a routine or a mental checklist to make it go away, if that's what you mean. The thought just kind of hits me, and I just sit there feeling awful about it. I don't do anything specific to try and fix it in the moment, I just let it weigh on me.
Did something traumatic happen involving your brother that this thought is connected to?

Yes. About six months ago, we were on a job site together. We were wiring a new commercial building. I... I was the one who checked the breaker panel, or at least I thought I did. I told him it was clear. He grabbed a live wire and... he got electrocuted. He didn't make it. So, yeah, that's where the thought comes from.
Since the accident, have unwanted memories of what happened been coming back to you repeatedly, even when you do not want to think about it?

Yeah... they do. I'll just be in the middle of wiring a panel, or maybe I'll hear my nephew shut the garage door, and suddenly I'm right back there. I can actually smell the smoke and... and I see my brother. It's like the job site just drops out from under me. I definitely don't want to think about it, but it just happens anyway.
Since the accident, have you been avoiding reminders of what happened, such as the job site, electrical work, or talking about your brother?

Yeah, I do. I mean... I don't even go into my own garage anymore unless I absolutely have to. I also quit helping out with the electrical stuff at my church. I just can't be around it right now. And as for talking... if people start bringing up old car projects we used to work on, or... or they mention the fire from the accident, I shut them down fast. I just won't talk about it.
Since the accident, have you felt constantly on guard or watchful for danger?

I don't think so, no. I mean, I'm careful around electricity, obviously, because of what happened, but I wouldn't say I'm constantly on guard or looking out for danger in general. Just... just trying to get through the day, mostly.
Since the accident, have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yeah, it's been really bad. Most nights I just lie there in the dark, listening for any sound... like crackling noises or a car door shutting in the driveway. And when I finally do manage to fall asleep, I just jolt awake, completely soaked in sweat from dreaming about the garage. Once that happens, I can't get back to sleep before I have to get up for work.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient experienced the accidental traumatic death of his brother six months ago and subsequently developed recurrent intrusive memories and flashback-like experiences, trauma-related dreams, avoidance of reminders, persistent guilt and negative beliefs about being dangerous, sleep disturbance, and clinically significant occupational and social impairment.
